correctness.rationale: The stated table has A²=T⊕W, A³=W=Ann(A), A⁴=0; A² acts trivially on the left and yz+zy is in W, so the Zinbiel identity follows. To verify the annihilator, right multiplication by u_i detects both active u_i,v_i coefficients, then left multiplication by u_i detects the t_i coefficients. Derivations preserve A² and W. For i≠j, differentiating u_i t_j=0 gives a s_j+b w+c s_i=0, killing the u_j,v_j components of D(u_i) and the t_i component of D(t_j); differentiating v_i t_j=0 does the same for D(v_i). Now the u_j u_i and u_j v_i equations eliminate the off-branch t_j components. Differentiating t_i=u_i v_i, w=u_i² and s_i=u_i t_i keeps their images in their branch, so branch projection gives a derivation of the five-dimensional table. Independent base calculation: write D(u)=a u+b v+c t and D(v)=d u+e v+f t modulo W. Comparing D(u²) and D(v²) forces c=0, 2a=2e+f. Differentiating uv+vu=0 yields f=0 and d=-b; then e=a and D(t)=2a t. Differentiating vt=w gives 2a w=3a w-b s, hence a=b=0 and all square images vanish. This applies also to k=1. Conversely any map A/A²→W is a derivation, giving dimension 2k(k+1); locality forces the same constraints pointwise. Every ideal containing an element outside W contains w: apply v_i(xv_i), v_i(xu_i), or v_ix according to which active coordinate is nonzero. In a direct-sum decomposition one ideal would consequently lie in W, while A², containing W, would lie in the other, a contradiction. This is a characteristic-zero proof for every k; the archived finite modular checks are not used as proof.

value.rationale: It answers the motivating paper's explicit unbounded indecomposable-existence question by producing a concrete family and computing its full linear derivation space.
